title: Wrap Curve
tagline: Wrap flat curves onto a curved profile by arc length -- length along the profile kept, height and width carried over.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Planforms, graphics, inlays and insert lines are drawn flat; the ski is built on a rockered, cambered profile. Native Wrap only handles cylinders and cones, and projecting foreshortens. Wrap Curve keeps the arc length along the profile, so a station 1500 mm along the layout lands 1500 mm along the ski.
useWhen: Put flat layout lines on the profile
Keep stations at their true distance along the ski
slides.caption: Tip example: 1200 flat + R600 tip; x = 1500 lands 300 into the arc.

points.head: Arc length kept
points.body: A point s along the From reference lands s along the To reference (a shift, no scaling).

points.head: Height and width kept
points.body: The point's offsets in the frame carry over: ribs stay perpendicular.

points.head: Layers bend
points.body: At height h around radius R they stretch or shrink by (R - h) / R, as a real layer does.

points.head: Frenet (default)
points.body: One normal carried along with minimal rotation: no flip at inflections.

points.head: Binormal
points.body: Normal from a plane you give (face or mate connector); every edge must lie in it.

points.head: Past the ends
points.body: The osculating circle continues the chain -- exact on arcs.

items.head: Flip normal
items.body: If 'up' comes out on the wrong side -- older models may need it after the 2026-09-23 frame change.

items.head: Only To flips
items.body: From's direction comes from its chain; an off-centre From reference pushes points past an end.

items.head: Break spans
items.body: Changes topology (more edges) -- downstream references may move.
